official_scoring_enabled_note: ENABLED 2026-07-31 (go-live, Amendment 31). Flipped to true together with reference_baseline.publication_allowed and token_fidelity_gate_status=implemented, so Yukon's baseline validation (which dispatches a scored run) can pass and the track can be imported/opened. The go-live prerequisites this attests are satisfied: hidden goldens + paired M5 baseline + weight manifests provisioned on m5-bench against the real Laguna weights (tokenizer vocab 100352); the 8-entry timed_prompt_pool populated, uploaded and probe-verified; and the token_fidelity_gate fully specified and signed off (status implemented). To take the track back offline, flip these three fields back and Yukon will refuse scored runs again at 'Enforce DFlash track enablement'.
timed_prompt_pool_note: Contract layer L6 (anti-lottery). The timed target is sampled UNIFORMLY AT RANDOM from this pool once per ranked run, from kernel entropy the participant cannot see or influence; the selected index is recorded only in the private audit dir. A single frozen timed prompt would make a failed ranked run free to retry, degrading every output-side gate into submit-until-green and letting a drafter-confidence threshold be tuned across resubmissions; sampling from a pool of N reduces that to a 1/N chance per attempt. Each entry must be an object {r2_path, sha256, bytes, noop_decode_speedup} and is verified byte-for-byte after download; noop_decode_speedup is the entry's pinned no-op reference that the trusted scoring step divides by (Amendment 32) and fails closed on if missing or non-positive. CURRENT STATE (2026-07-31): EIGHT distinct entries, one per domain -- science (Darwin), history (Herodotus), biography (Plutarch), empiricist philosophy (Hume), analytic philosophy (Russell), political philosophy (Plato), drama (Sophocles), economics (Adam Smith). Each is a low-memorization prose seed continued by the reference at K=2 over 512 rows; the original single lowsim-prose entry was DROPPED to decouple this pool from the live serial competition (its seed was the serial correctness prompt) and because it was an outlier-hard prompt. All eight passed the degeneracy screen (.github/scripts/check-dflash-golden-degeneracy.sh: seed variety >= 0.40, >= 1 near-tie row, min top-2 gap <= 1.0), and their measured no-op speedups cluster tightly at 0.8726-0.8939 (2.4% spread, worst = Russell 0.8726), which is what the decode floor is derived from. NOTE ON CHARACTER: these are moderate-difficulty prose (draft acceptance ~75%), not the deliberately low-similarity, low-acceptance material the target-id lowsim-prose-v1 name implies; a harder benchmark would need curated low-similarity prompts. Three separate checks in the selection step of .github/workflows/dflash-benchmark.yml keep this safe: it fails CLOSED on pool_size < 1; it rejects the whole dispatch if ANY entry is malformed (missing/empty r2_path, sha256 that is not a 64-character lowercase hex digest, or bytes that is not a positive integer), checked over EVERY entry before sampling rather than only the sampled one; and it REFUSES A RANKED RUN unless there are at least 8 DISTINCT sha256 digests AND at least 8 DISTINCT r2_path keys. The floor counts distinctness, not length: listing one golden eight times has length 8 and anti-lottery value zero. Hashes here were computed from the generated golden files that the operator uploads byte-for-byte to these r2_path keys; the workflow re-verifies each sha256 after download, so a mismatch (wrong upload) fails closed. To grow or refresh the pool, re-derive BOTH the floor (from the worst per-prompt no-op) AND the block size across the whole pool at the ranked window.

Unlike the retired 4-bit placeholder this manifest is fully populated and byte-verified (13 entries) and is the SAME manifest the live serial track uses, so the DFlash track reuses the already-provisioned reference checkpoint cache.

The draft is provisioned as the operator-repacked BF16 MLX artifact (fused qkv split, BF16 PRESERVED -- the drafter is NOT quantized; see quantization_note): 924137156-byte model.safetensors + 1121-byte config.json = 924138277 bytes (expected_bytes), confirmed against the M5-generated manifest. An earlier plan to convert to MLX affine 4-bit at setup was DROPPED.
assistant.maximum_total_bytes_note: 1 GiB budget: headroom over the ~924 MB BF16 MLX repack (924138277 bytes total) that setup downloads and verifies against the pinned manifest; the drafter stays BF16 (no quantization).
assistant.quantization_note: The pinned upstream draft ships BF16 (torch_dtype bfloat16). It is repacked to MLX layout by Vendor/mlx-swift-lm/scripts/convert_laguna_dflash.py with BF16 PRESERVED -- the drafter is NOT quantized. (The retired track's plan to convert it to affine 4-bit group-64 on-box was dropped: at 924 MB the drafter is cheap to keep in BF16, and quantizing it would add draft-side error that lowers the accept rate without materially reducing memory.)

protocol.name: trusted_dflash_block_v1
protocol.maximum_block_size_note: Raised from 4 (Gemma-MTP assistant era) to 16: the DFlash draft model's config block_size is 16 and it drafts a whole masked block in one forward. SUPERSEDED MEASUREMENT: an earlier note here claimed peak decode speedup at K=8 (1.60x) with K=16 at 1.53x. Those came from short and/or self-generated prompts and do NOT reproduce at the frozen window. Measured at a 512-token seed over 128 decode steps with matched token counts on both sides: on varied prose, draft acceptance is 69% and K=4 is 0.840x, i.e. SLOWER than serial; on a degenerate greedy self-continuation (122 distinct tokens in 512) acceptance is ~100% and K=4 is 1.117x. A verify row costs only ~10% less than a standalone serial step, so break-even needs draft acceptance above ~92%. K remains a runtime choice bounded by this maximum, but do not read the maximum as a recommendation.
protocol.decode_tokens_note: The RANKED decode window, in parent-counted tokens. Was 128 (inherited from the retired track's local-iterate default) while proposed_scoring.ranked_decode_window_tokens and benchmark.json scoring.decodeTokens both said 512 -- three places disagreeing about the scored window. All three must stay equal; DFlashTrackTests pins that. maximum_decode_tokens (1536) remains the protocol ceiling, and the local scripts use their own smaller values for directional runs.

reference_baseline._note: HISTORY: the paired serial K=1 baseline, floor calibration, and hidden goldens for Laguna XS 2.1 had to be established on m5-bench before publication could flip (go-live runbook steps B-C); satisfied at go-live 2026-07-31 (Amendment 31), when publication_allowed flipped true with status rebaselined_m5.

proposed_scoring.score: dflash_decode_speedup = (paired_serial_decode_sec_per_token / dflash_decode_sec_per_token) / noop_reference[sampled_prompt] -- the raw ratio-of-means paired speedup, NORMALISED by the sampled prompt's own pinned no-op reference (timed_prompt_pool[].noop_decode_speedup). Normalisation (Amendment 32) makes every pool prompt's no-op map to 1.0, so per-prompt difficulty (the 2.4% no-op spread the anti-lottery sampler would otherwise inject into the ranked score) is removed and run-to-run variance collapses to measurement noise (<0.5%). See normalized_scoring below.
proposed_scoring.aggregation: ratio_of_means: mean(serial seconds/token across accepted pairs) / mean(dflash seconds/token across accepted pairs)
proposed_scoring.paired_serial_reference: trusted serial K=1 target decode (probe path) over the same golden, same session, same thermal gate, same box
proposed_scoring.denominator_authority: trusted parent wall time divided by the parent-configured decode total
proposed_scoring.component_floor: NORMALISED aggregate dflash_decode_speedup >= 0.95 (adopted 2026-08-01, Amendment 32): the ratio-of-means aggregate is divided by the sampled prompt's pinned no-op reference (timed_prompt_pool[].noop_decode_speedup) so every pool prompt's no-op maps to 1.0, and 0.95 = 1.0 x 0.952 applies a uniform 'within 5% of this prompt's own no-op' threshold to EVERY prompt (the same 0.952 competitive margin used by every prior derivation, now applied per-prompt instead of only to the worst prompt; see normalized_scoring). HISTORY (raw, pre-normalisation): the floor was a single RAW threshold 0.83, derived 2026-07-31 from the WORST measured no-op across the whole 8-prompt timed_prompt_pool, at the ranked window (512 decode tokens, K=2, the exact values the workflow dispatches). Each of the 8 pool entries was measured no-op end-to-end on M5 (512-token seed, 512 parent-counted decode tokens, matched token counts, 40C entry gate, ratio-of-means, PARITY_OK per entry); the aggregates cluster tightly: Russell 0.8726 (WORST), Plutarch 0.8822, Herodotus 0.8833, Darwin 0.8834, Plato 0.8848, Sophocles 0.8891, Smith 0.8921, Hume 0.8939 -- a 2.4% spread. Floor = worst 0.8726 x 0.952 = 0.8307, floored to 0.83 (4.9% margin above the worst no-op; run-to-run spread is under 0.5%). 0.952 is the margin every derivation of this floor has used. Because the pool no-ops are tightly clustered, a single global floor is nearly per-prompt-exact here and the anti-lottery gap is small (unlike the earlier mixed material). THREE superseded derivations, each measured under conditions that were not the ranked ones: 0.80 (2026-07-30, 0.840x at ~69% acceptance on a different golden, rejected a correct no-op); 0.52 (0.5493 at K=3 over a 128-token window -- s/token ratios do not transfer across window lengths because the seed prefill is charged inside the decode window); 0.55 (0.5882 at the ranked window but from a SINGLE deliberately-hard lowsim prompt at ~34% acceptance, since dropped from the pool). PROVISIONAL on the pool's character: this pool is moderate-difficulty prose (~75% draft acceptance), not the low-acceptance lowsim character the target-id name implies; a harder benchmark would lower this floor and needs curated low-similarity prompts. To grow or refresh the pool, re-derive BOTH the per-prompt no-op references AND the block size across the whole pool at the ranked window. The durable fix flagged here -- normalising each prompt by its own measured no-op -- is now ADOPTED (Amendment 32, normalized_scoring), so this floor is enforced on the NORMALISED aggregate and the ranked score no longer depends on which prompt the sampler drew. MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEEDUP stays 5.0. This NORMALISED value must stay equal to scoring.decodeSpeedupFloor in benchmark.json and to MLXFAST_DFLASH_DECODE_SPEEDUP_FLOOR in the workflow (all three pinned equal by test). The box wrapper's MIN_ACCEPTED_SPEEDUP in /opt/bench-runner/measure-dflash-job.sh is DECOUPLED from this value to a LOOSE RAW measurement-sanity floor of 0.50 (APPLIED 2026-08-01 on the serving box: root inode-preserving edit, backup .pre-decouple050, manifest re-signed, janitor audit clean), because the box measures raw speedup and does not know the normalisation reference; the raw 0.83 it previously enforced would false-reject a Russell-drawn candidate whose raw speedup sits in [0.829, 0.83) but normalises to >= 0.95 (the Amendment 28 failure mode).

normalized_scoring.rationale: The anti-lottery sampler draws one pool prompt uniformly at random per ranked run. The pool's no-op speedups span 0.8726-0.8939 (2.4%), so before normalisation a submission's ranked score swung up to ~2.4% purely from which prompt was drawn -- dwarfing the <0.5% run-to-run measurement noise. Dividing each run's raw ratio-of-means paired speedup by the sampled prompt's own pinned no-op reference makes every prompt's no-op map to 1.0, collapsing the difficulty component to measurement noise while PRESERVING random sampling (the anti-lottery property is unpredictable, unbiasable selection -- not post-hoc secrecy). A single global raw floor (the retired 0.83) was correct only for the worst prompt and lenient for the rest; the normalised floor 0.95 is a uniform per-prompt threshold.
normalized_scoring.reference_source: timed_prompt_pool[].noop_decode_speedup, keyed by sha256. Each is the prompt's UNMODIFIED end-to-end no-op ratio-of-means at the ranked window (512 decode tokens, K=2, matched token counts, 40C entry gate, PARITY_OK per entry), measured on m5-bench. These are pinned reference constants, not per-run measurements; they are tied to the pinned reference baseline and must be re-pinned if the baseline, window, K, or pool changes.
normalized_scoring.applied_at: .github/workflows/dflash-benchmark.yml step 'Compute DFlash score and enforce floor', which looks up the sampled prompt's reference by sha256 from the TRUSTED contract checkout (fixtures/laguna_xs_2_1_dflash_track.json in GITHUB_WORKSPACE, NOT the candidate-writable job workspace copy -- fixtures/ is outside editablePaths), computes normalized = raw_ratio_of_means / reference, and enforces component_floor on the normalised value. Fails closed if the sampled sha256 has no pinned reference or the reference is not a positive number.
normalized_scoring.published_score: score = normalised ratio-of-means. metrics carry BOTH the raw ratio-of-means (dflash_decode_speedup_ratio_of_means) and the reference used (noop_reference_decode_speedup), plus the normalised value (dflash_decode_speedup_normalized == score), for full audit. Because raw and reference are both auditable and the per-prompt references are public here, the sampled prompt is post-hoc inferable from a published near-no-op run -- this does NOT weaken anti-lottery (selection stays unpredictable and unbiasable) and matches the pre-existing inferability from the already-published per-side seconds/token means.
normalized_scoring.box_gate_decoupled: MIN_ACCEPTED_SPEEDUP in /opt/bench-runner/measure-dflash-job.sh is DECOUPLED from this ranked (normalised) floor to a LOOSE RAW measurement-sanity lower bound of 0.50, because the box measures raw speedup and has no reference. APPLIED 2026-08-01 on the serving box (root inode-preserving edit, backup measure-dflash-job.sh.pre-decouple050, gen-manifest.sh re-sign, janitor --audit-only clean); the raw 0.83 it previously enforced could false-reject a Russell-drawn candidate with raw in [0.829, 0.83) that normalises to >= 0.95. Any ADDITIONAL box brought to serve this track must apply the same decouple. The ranked floor is enforced NORMALISED in the trusted workflow. MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SPEEDUP stays raw on the box.

proposed_scoring.token_fidelity_gate: PROPOSED SPEC (2026-07-31, awaiting operator sign-off; merging this text adopts nothing -- the go-live lock is tokenFidelityGateStatus in benchmark.json, which stays below 'implemented' until the operator flips it at runbook Step D, and trackCannotBeEnabledWhileTheFidelityGateIsUnspecified fails the build if official_scoring_enabled goes true first). Supersedes the Gemma-MTP bit_exact_gate, whose criterion -- every returned token exactly matches the trusted SEQUENTIAL oracle -- is empirically unachievable for DFlash on Laguna NVFP4: the target's own block-shaped forward diverges from K sequential forwards at near-tie argmax positions with NO drafter involved (M5 2026-07-30: 14/14 observed divergences were target block-vs-sequential; max sequential-logit gap at a divergence 0.625; 12/14 were sequential rank 2, one rank 3, one rank 5 in a flat distribution). THE GATE, as implemented in Sources/MLXFastTrustedHarness/LagunaRuntimeDFlash.swift and exercised live: (1) SCOPE -- every emitted token of every round is re-verified in the trusted parent against a reference teacher-forced on the candidate's own emitted prefix (so a divergent token re-anchors every later row to the candidate's actual chain); declared rows are re-checked in full and the rejected tail is priced (Amendment 21); no report publishes without the reference pass (requireReferenceValidated -- fail closed). (2) ADMISSION LADDER, per emitted token, first match wins: (a) EXACT -- the token equals the reference's K=1 sequential argmax; (b) DECLARED-FRAME -- the token is the reference's own argmax at the block width the candidate declared (contract layer L1); (c) NEAR-TIE, budgeted -- the reference's own logit for the emitted token sits within the measured drift envelope of the reference's own top-1: reference_top1_logit - reference_logit(emitted) <= 4.875, where 4.875 = 2 x 2.4375, twice the maximum live candidate-vs-reference top-2 logit delta measured under post-run replay across widths, fixtures and seeds (Amendment 16; the multiplier is 2 because reordering two logits needs a gap below the difference of two per-logit drifts; the motivating 0.625 sequential-gap measurement sits well inside it). The logits are the REFERENCE's own, so a submission can neither manufacture a flat row nor learn which positions are flat without doing the reference's work; a golden row that predates the emitted-token-logit fields falls back to Amendment 14's top-2 membership form, and an emitted-token logit recorded for a different token admits nothing. (d) RESIDUAL, budgeted -- a top-2 member at a row the reference answers confidently: genuine candidate-vs-reference drift, which Amendment 20 measured occupying the band (12,800 comparisons), so its budget is small but not zero. (e) Anything else is tokenNotAdmissible and the run is REJECTED. (3) BUDGETS, scaled per thousand scored tokens, rounded up, enforced by the residualBudgetExhausted violation: near-tie 40/1000 (21 slots at the ranked 512-token window; 6 at the 128-token diagnostic window) and residual 5/1000 (3 slots at 512). Exhausting either rejects the run; a divergence outside the envelope is never admissible under any budget. (4) MEASURED STATE at the shipping configuration (K=2, 512 decode tokens, ranked hidden golden, M5-C, 2026-07-31 -- three consecutive runs plus gates-only CI run 30664724953): all_tokens_matched true in every run; the UNMODIFIED baseline consumes 9 of its 21 near-tie slots (43% -- the same 9 in all three runs, i.e. deterministic frame divergence, not noise) and 0 of 3 residual slots. Prior evidence run 30613617340 (2026-07-30, different golden): 512/512 rows admissible as 503 exact + 6 near-tie + 3 declared-frame, residual 0, max_top2_logit_delta 1.875 against the 4.875 tolerance. (5) KNOWN LIMITS the sign-off accepts (Amendment 29): the budget VALUE has never been probed near its limit (highest observed utilisation 9/21); the gate has never faced an adversarially-motivated candidate (Amendments 18-23 record gates that looked sound until first attacked); and near-tie consumption is a property of the timed MATERIAL (measured 0 per 128 rows on repetitive text, 3 per 128 on varied prose, 9 per 512 on the ranked golden), so whoever populates timed_prompt_pool MUST re-measure baseline utilisation on every entry and confirm headroom -- a pool prompt on which the unmodified baseline alone approaches the budget would reject honest candidates, the floor's Amendment 28 failure mode transplanted to fidelity. The 8-prompt pool populated 2026-07-31 (Amendment 30) HAS this per-entry baseline-utilisation measurement: every entry's no-op consumes 0 of 21 near-tie slots and 0 of 3 residual slots (511-512 of 512 tokens exact), i.e. maximal fidelity headroom -- moderate-difficulty prose produces far fewer block-vs-sequential near-ties than the dropped lowsim entry (which alone consumed 9/21). The enforcing constants live in MLXFastCore's Constants.swift (experimentalDFlashNearTieLogitEnvelope, experimentalDFlashNearTieAdmissionBudgetPerThousand, experimentalDFlashResidualDivergenceBudgetPerThousand) and this text is pinned to them by test, so prose and implementation cannot drift apart silently.
proposed_scoring.stall_guardrail: a run whose max block latency exceeds 4x its p50 block latency is rejected as measurement-invalid with one gated retry
proposed_scoring.prefill_component: none; seed prefill is charged inside the decode measurement
proposed_scoring.leaderboard: separate laguna-xs-2.1-dflash-v1 namespace, never mixed with the serial track
proposed_scoring.measurement_protocol: minimum three accepted thermal-gated pairs per session (target four) with alternating order; single-pair scores are not publishable
